style: who is speaking to whom, and what has just happened

candidates.angle: The repeated word yaanti means go to, showing that worship lands on its target.
Krishna calls himself the enjoyer and lord, then says others worship other beings.
candidates.evidence: For I am the enjoyer and lord of all sacrifices. But those people do not know me in truth, and so they fall away.

candidates.angle: The word mamam means me, and it marks the final destination for those devoted to Krishna.
candidates.evidence: मद्याजिनोऽपि माम् (those devoted to me come to me)

angle_en: Mamam: the destination for those devoted only to Krishna
angle_hi: मामम्: केवल मेरी ओर भक्ति करने वालों की मंज़िल

en.intro: Krishna has just said he is the true lord of all worship, and that people who do not know him fall away. Now he explains where different kinds of worship lead.
en.notice: Listen to the word mamam, me, at the end of the verse. It is the destination for those whose devotion is aimed only at me, while other devotions reach other ends.
en.next: Krishna then says he accepts even a simple leaf, flower, fruit, or water, if offered with devotion.
en.meaning: Those devoted to the radiant beings reach the radiant beings. Those devoted to the ancestors reach the ancestors. Those devoted to spirits reach the spirits. But those devoted to me come to me.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने अभी कहा है कि वे ही सभी यज्ञों के स्वामी हैं, और जो लोग उन्हें नहीं जानते वे गिर जाते हैं। अब वे बताते हैं कि अलग-अलग पूजाएँ कहाँ ले जाती हैं।
hi.meaning: देवताओं का पूजन करनेवाले देवताओं को प्राप्त होते हैं, पितरों का पूजन करनेवाले पितरों को, भूत-प्रेतों का पूजन करनेवाले भूत-प्रेतों को, परन्तु मेरा पूजन करनेवाले मुझे ही प्राप्त होते हैं।
hi.notice: अंत में एक शब्द सुनिए, मामम्, अर्थात् मैं। यह उनके लिए मंज़िल है जिनकी भक्ति केवल मेरी ओर है, जबकि बाकी पूजाएँ अपने-अपने स्थानों पर ले जाती हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण आगे कहते हैं कि वे एक पत्ते, फूल, फल या जल भी स्वीकार करते हैं, यदि वह भक्ति भाव से दिया गया हो।

issues: meaning_changed: "अंत में एक शब्द सुनिए, मामम्, अर्थात् मैं।" (The Hindi translation in the source uses 'पूजन' (worship), while the notice in the script uses 'ध्यान' (meditation/attention). While not a direct contradiction, the shift from 'worship' to 'meditation' changes the semantic nuance of the verse, which is about active worship (yajña) rather than just passive meditation.)

meaning_changed: "अंत में एक शब्द सुनिए, मामम्, अर्थात् मैं। यही एकमात्र मंज़िल है जो बदलती नहीं है।" (The Hindi meaning of 'mamam' is 'मैं' (I). The notice claims this is the only destination that does not change. However, the source text and previous verse (24) state that Krishna is the true lord/enjoyer of all sacrifices, implying all worship ultimately reaches him. The notice contradicts the established context by saying mamam is the only unchanging destination, when the broader narrative says all worship is aimed at him.)
